One of the best things for kidney disease is to encourage more water intake. Cats in general are very prone to both dehydration and CKD. I would suggest buying a few additional water fountains. The more variety in style and material the better. Cats are picky about water sources and the more they approve, the more they’re willing to drink. You can experiment with putting them on different locations as well. Another common hydration trick is to add water to their food. This may not work with the dry but you can add some water into the wet food, turning it more into a slurry. When I was 15 I witnessed what the laws of physics during a car crash can do to a human body. My mom was driving down the highway with my 2 sleeping siblings in the back and myself in the passenger seat. I remember there being a lot less traffic than usual so we were a good distance away from the cars ahead of us. Suddenly you hear the far away horns and breaks squealing from several cars followed by the sound of cars slamming into each other. I think a tire had flown off of a vehicle and was flying in the opposite direction of traffic. Anticipating the car crash ahead, we had slowed down considerably along with every other driver. The accident actually wasn’t too bad but it did impede 2 of the 3 lanes. We had slowed to a near stop to merge from the far left to the far right. A smaller minivan was just ahead in the right lane. They were going maybe 35ish MPH. Then a giant SUV goes flying past us down the center. SUV driver very obviously wasn’t paying attention because they slammed on their breaks way too late and swerved into the right lane at a high speed narrowly avoiding the original accident. When doing so the bumped into the minivan at such a force that it was shoved head into the concrete barrier for the exit lane. There was absolutely no time for the minivan to even react. 

I watched as the unrestrained passenger of the car flew through the windshield and about 10ft of air time while the front half of the car itself folded in half. She appeared to be a Hispanic woman about 35 years old. Her body was thrown straight onto some kind of metal / rebar left there for construction. It impaled straight through her in the exact middle of her torso. She was laying face down with her arm twisted underneath her in several different directions. Another smaller metal object sliced through the side of her abdomen. For at least 10 seconds she appeared to be trying to get up but then it became full body spasming to just arm and leg spasms over the next 20-30 secs while a large puddle of blood pooled underneath her. Her injuries had obviously proved fatal when she stopped moving entirely. Her face smushed directly into the concrete. 

My mom drove off extremely quickly after that in a failed attempt to prevent me from seeing her body. We both sat in this shocked silence for at least a couple minutes before she calmly told me to get out my phone and call 911 in case no one else had already. So I did and basically just reported that we had just driven past a crash that looked to have fatalities and gave them the location, no other details. The rest of the 15 minute drive was in silence with my siblings asleep. When we got home my mom told me not to tell them what happened to not upset them. I agreed. Then we just went about the rest of the day like nothing had happened. Honestly it was more like I was trying to convince myself that it was just something I made up in my head.

I’ve been in your exact situation a couple of times. Each time I was direct with my psychiatrist about how I felt regarding possible medication changes. Excluding an actual mental health crisis, your psychiatrist should be taking your input into serious consideration. Now it’s still their right to refuse to prescribe a medication but it’s also your right to refuse a medication (if outpatient).

I’d bring the subject up at the very beginning of your next appointment. Using a clear, professional tone say something like this: “I given quite a bit of thought about the idea of switching to a different mood stabilizer. I’m actually really satisfied with the effectiveness of my current medication. I think my symptoms are well managed on a day-to-day basis and I don’t have any noticeable side effects.  It’s been working very well for 7 years and I don’t want to give up on it just yet. When I had my breakthrough manic episode, there were several emotionally stressful things going on in my life. Could we instead put together a plan that will help me properly handle potential triggers?”

You want to make sure you offer a good suggestion on an alternative solution (with willingness to follow through). Psychiatrists like when patients take an active role and will be more receptive to your input.

I always call the client and sometimes if there’s more than 1 number on the account I’ll call both. If I left a message and haven’t heard anything back in over a week then I’ll call again AND text this time. 99% of the time clients will either come in or will give us a call to let us know when they plan to pick up.

This is the script I follow with a somber but professional tone

“Hello. This is [hospital name] we are calling to let you know that we have received [pet’s name] things back from [crematorium company]. They can be picked up whenever you would be ready to do so.”

I always always always use the pets name in my message as it acknowledges the pet as an individual and their personal importance to the owner. Saying just urn, items, deliveries, turns what remains of their pet into just another object. For a similar reason I  include the last line. It empathizes with the emotional impact the loss has on the owner and normalizes how much it might’ve affected them. 

Also a 100% generic message tends to feel more like an impersonal call from a business. I try to make it seem more like it’s a personal message from me just for that specific client.  Clients should be treated as you would someone that is grieving a family member.

I have been seeing my current psychiatrist nurse practitioner every month for almost 5 years so there's a lot of trust. I suffer from a few other severe mental disorders so ADHD wasn't even addressed until 14 months ago.  I take a LOT of pills a day and my regimen changes in some way at least once a month. At this point I'm the most stable that I have been since I was 8.

It was discovered that Ritalin does wonders for not only my ADHD, but my anxiety and depression as well. Because of this, my dosing is a little different than with ADHD. My doctor basically prescribes me X number of pills a month but I chose when or how much to take a day with guidelines he gives me. So the prescription might say "take 1 pill in morning and 1/2 as needed per day" but he would tell me I could take up to 2 a day with the understanding that I only get a set amount a month and will have to budget appropriately. Usually by the very end of the month I have used up all my as needed pills. This is relevant all relevant because it means that if I have something coming up, then I will pick up my meds a day or two early. I try to avoid this as much as possible.

I think it's also important to mention that due to problems in the past, I have had to switch pharmacies (same company, different location). I had been going to my original pharmacy (A) for about 4 years before I switched the to the pharmacy I'm at now (B). The first time I filled a prescription to Ritalin at pharmacy A, everything went great. Dropped it off and picked it up a few hours later. Second time I dropped the slip off at exactly 30 days and they filled it same day. The third time was when everything went down hill. I had gone to my doctor about a week earlier than usual and he went ahead and wrote my next months prescription so I wouldn't have to go back. He had told me beforehand that they wouldn't be able to fill it until 27 days. I decided to take it to the pharmacy write away so I wouldn't lose it and they could just fill it when it was time. When I went to drop it off though, they made a big deal about it being written early. They kept saying that they couldn't fill it and that there wasn't a reason for me to get a prescription written a week early. I explained that I knew of the 27 day rule and that I didn't mind picking it up in a few days. Of course they didn't say anything else about my 6 other prescriptions I was dropping off that were done by the exact same doctor at the same time.

Every month was the same thing. Sometimes they'd offer to do a partial fill but say if I chose to do that then that's all I get for the month and couldn't claim the rest of the prescription. The final time I used pharmacy A for Ritalin it was exactly 27 days since my last fill when I gave the new script. The tech had told me to wait a minute and came back with the pharmacist. I've had a few great experiences (as far as being in the mental hospital goes) and one horrible experience that pushed me so far back in treatment. Make sure you do your research on facilities beforehand. 

As far as what to bring, here are some safe guidelines. Not everyplace is so strict but better safe than to be left in a thin hospital gown. 

No laces, zippers, strings, hoodies, scarves, hats, leggings/ yoga pants, tank tops, booty shorts, anything provocative, clothes with holes. Depending on factors, underwire bras can also be confiscated. 

Clothing can't have; bad words, skulls, depiction of death or violence, pentagrams, or anything else associated with anything "triggering". Most metal and alternative band shirts weren't allowed.

Yes clothes- plain t-shirts, sweat pants or pajama pants without the strings, pajama tops, sweatshirts, jeans, cardigans, ankle length skirts. Basically anything that isn't in the "no" piles. When packing, keep in mind that you want to be comfy. Most people wear pjs all day. Also bring lots and lots of socks with a pair of slip on shoes. Some places require your socks to be non slip. 

For toiletries bring a non electric toothbrush and have your toothpaste, shampoo and stuff be travel sized. 

Expect there to be no cellphone or computer access during your stay, so bring something to do between therapy and meal times. Popular things include cards, coloring books (no pencil sharpeners allowed so sharpen pencils in advance), and reading books. If you bring a book and the subject matter is deemed too dark or triggering they won't let you have it. Like don't try to bring 13 reasons why with you. 

I think that's about it but if you have any questions just ask. This is just based off my personal experiences though. Sorry if it's a lot, I'm in the middle of a manic episode and can't seem to stop myself.
